vsm2.14:153.1:
153. (xxxi) Specific neutrality (tatra-majjhattatā—lit. "neutrality in regard thereto") is neutrality
(majjhattatā) in regard to those states of consciousness and consciousness-concomitants arisen in association with it.
vsm2.14:153.2: It has the characteristic of conveying consciousness and consciousness-concomitants evenly.
vsm2.14:153.3: Its function is to prevent deficiency and excess, or its function is to inhibit partiality.
vsm2.14:153.5: It should be regarded as like a conductor (driver) who looks with equanimity on thoroughbreds progressing evenly.
vsm2.14:154.1:
154. (xxxii)–(xxxiii) Compassion and gladness should be understood
as given in the Description of the Divine Abodes (IX.§92, 94, 95),
vsm2.14:154.2:
except that those are of the fine-material sphere and have attained to absorption,
while these are of the sense sphere. This is the only difference.
vsm2.14:154.3: Some, however, want to include among the inconstant both loving-kindness and equanimity. That cannot be accepted
vsm2.14:154.4: for, as to meaning, non-hate itself is loving-kindness, and specific neutrality is equanimity.
vsm2.14:155.1:
155. (xxxiv)–(xxxvi) Abstinence from bodily misconduct: the compound kāyaduccaritavirati
resolves as kāyaduccaritato virati; so also with the other two.
vsm2.14:155.2:
But as regards characteristic, etc., these three have the characteristic of non-transgression in the respective
fields of bodily conduct, etc.; they have the characteristic of not treading there, is what is said.
vsm2.14:155.3: Their function is to draw back from the fields of bodily misconduct, and so on.
vsm2.14:155.4: They are manifested as the not doing of these things.
vsm2.14:155.5: Their proximate causes are the special qualities of faith, conscience, shame, fewness of wishes, and so on.
vsm2.14:155.6: They should be regarded as the mind's averseness from evil-doing.
vsm2.14:156.1:
156. So these are the thirty-six formations that should be understood to come into association with the first
profitable consciousness of the sense sphere (1).
vsm2.14:156.2: And as with the first, so with the second (2), the only difference here being promptedness.
vsm2.14:156.3: (3)–(4) Those associated with the third (3) should be understood as all the foregoing except non-delusion (xv).
vsm2.14:156.4: Likewise with the fourth (4), the only difference here being promptedness.
vsm2.14:156.5: (5)–(6) All those stated in the first instance, except happiness (v), come into association with the fifth (5).
vsm2.14:156.6: Likewise with the sixth (6), the only difference here being promptedness.
vsm2.14:156.7: (7)–(8) Those associated with the seventh (7) should be understood as the last except non-delusion (xv).
vsm2.14:156.8: Likewise with the eighth (8), the only difference here being promptedness.
vsm2.14:157.1:
157. (9)–(13) All those stated in the first instance, except the three abstinences (xxxiv-xxxvi),
come into association with the first of the fine-material profitable kinds of consciousness (9).
vsm2.14:157.2: With the second (10) applied thought (iii) is also lacking.
vsm2.14:157.3: With the third (11) sustained thought (iv) is also lacking.
vsm2.14:157.4: With the fourth (12) happiness (v) is also lacking.
vsm2.14:157.5: With the fifth (13) compassion (xxxii) and gladness (xxxiii), among the inconstant, are also lacking.
vsm2.14:157.6:
(14)–(17) In the case of the four kinds of immaterial profitable consciousness these are the same
as the last-mentioned, for it is only the immaterialness that is the difference here.
vsm2.14:158.1:
158. (18)–(21) As regards the supramundane, firstly, in the case of the path consciousness having the first jhāna
they should be understood to be as stated in the case of the first fine-material-sphere consciousness (9).
vsm2.14:158.2:
The paths classed as belonging to the second jhāna, etc., should be understood to be as stated in the cases
respectively of the second fine-material-sphere jhāna, and so on (10)– (13).
vsm2.14:158.3:
But the difference here is absence of compassion (xxxii) and gladness (xxxiii),
constancy of the abstinences (xxxiv-xxxvi), and supramundaneness.
vsm2.14:159.1:
159. II. (22) As regards the unprofitable, there are firstly seventeen associated with the first unprofitable consciousness
rooted in greed (22), that is to say, thirteen constant given in the texts as such (see Dhs § 365) and four or-whatever-states.
vsm2.14:159.2:
Herein, the thirteen given as such are these: contact (i), volition (ii), applied thought (iii),
sustained thought (iv), happiness (v), energy (vi), life (vii), concentration (viii), (xxxvii) consciencelessness,
(xxxviii) shamelessness, (xxxix) greed, (xl) delusion, (xli) wrong view.
vsm2.14:159.3: The four or-whatever-states are these: zeal (xxviii), resolution (xxix), (xlii) agitation, attention (xxx).
vsm2.14:160.1: 160. Herein, (xxxvii) it has no conscientious scruples, thus it is consciencelessness.
vsm2.14:160.2: (xxxviii) It is unashamed, thus it is shamelessness.
vsm2.14:160.3:
Of these, consciencelessness has the characteristic of absence of disgust at bodily misconduct,
etc., or it has the characteristic of immodesty.
vsm2.14:160.4:
Shamelessness has the characteristic of absence of dread on their account, or it
has the characteristic of absence of anxiety about them.
vsm2.14:160.6: The detail, however, is the opposite of what was said above under conscience (xi) and shame (xii).
vsm2.14:161.1: 161. (xxxix) By its means they are greedy, or it itself is greedy, or it is just the mere being greedy, thus is it greed.
vsm2.14:161.2: (xl) By its means they are deluded, or it itself is deluded, or it is just the mere being deluded, thus it is delusion.
vsm2.14:162.1: 162. Of these, greed has the characteristic of grasping an object, like birdlime (lit. "monkey lime").
vsm2.14:162.2: Its function is sticking, like meat put in a hot pan.
vsm2.14:162.3: It is manifested as not giving up, like the dye of lamp-black.
vsm2.14:162.4: Its proximate cause is seeing enjoyment in things that lead to bondage.
vsm2.14:162.5:
Swelling with the current of craving, it should be regarded as taking beings with it to states of loss,
as a swift-flowing river does to the great ocean.
vsm2.14:163.1: 163. Delusion has the characteristic of blindness, or it has the characteristic of unknowing.
vsm2.14:163.2: Its function is non-penetration, or its function is to conceal the individual essence of an object.
vsm2.14:163.3: It is manifested as the absence of right theory (see Ch. XVII, §52), or it is manifested as darkness.
vsm2.14:163.4: Its proximate cause is unwise (unjustified) attention.
vsm2.14:163.5: It should be regarded as the root of all that is unprofitable.
vsm2.14:164.1: 164. (xli) By its means they see wrongly, or it itself sees wrongly, or it is just the mere seeing wrongly, thus it is wrong view.
vsm2.14:164.4: It is manifested as wrong interpreting.
vsm2.14:164.5: Its proximate cause is unwillingness to see Noble Ones, and so on.
vsm2.14:164.6: It should be regarded as the most reprehensible of all.
vsm2.14:165.2: It has the characteristic of disquiet, like water whipped by the wind.
vsm2.14:165.3: Its function is unsteadiness, like a flag or banner whipped by the wind.
vsm2.14:165.4: It is manifested as turmoil, like ashes flung up by pelting with stones.
vsm2.14:165.5: Its proximate cause is unwise attention to mental disquiet.
vsm2.14:165.6: It should be regarded as distraction of consciousness.
vsm2.14:166.1:
166. The remaining formations here should be understood as already stated under the profitable. For it
is only the unprofitableness that differentiates them as bad.
vsm2.14:166.2:
So these are the seventeen formations that should be understood to come into association with the first
unprofitable consciousness (22).
vsm2.14:166.3:
(23) And as with the first, so with the second (23), but here the difference
is promptedness and inconstant occurrence of (xliii) stiffening and torpor.
vsm2.14:167.1: 167. Herein, (xliii) stiffening (thīnanatā) is stiffness (thīna); making torpid (middhanatā) is torpor (middha).
vsm2.14:167.2: The meaning is, paralysis due to lack of urgency, and loss of vigour.
vsm2.14:167.3: The compound thīnamiddha (stiffness-and-torpor) should be resolved into thīnañ ca middhañ ca.
vsm2.14:167.4: Herein, stiffness has the characteristic of lack of driving power.
vsm2.14:167.5: Its function is to remove energy.
vsm2.14:167.7: Torpor has the characteristic of unwieldiness.
vsm2.14:167.9: It is manifested as laziness, or it is manifested as nodding and sleep.
vsm2.14:167.10: The proximate cause of both is unwise attention to boredom, sloth, and so on.
vsm2.14:168.1:
168. (24) With the third unprofitable consciousness (24) there should be understood to be associated
those given for the first (22), excepting wrong view (xli).
vsm2.14:168.2: But here the difference is that there is inconstant occurrence of (xliv) pride (conceit).
vsm2.14:168.3: That pride has the characteristic of haughtiness.
vsm2.14:168.5: It is manifested as vain gloriousness.
vsm2.14:168.6: Its proximate cause is greed dissociated from views.
vsm2.14:168.7: It should be regarded as like madness.
vsm2.14:168.8:
(25) With the fourth (25) should be understood to be associated those given for the second (23),
excepting wrong view (xli). And here pride (xliv) is among the inconstant too.
vsm2.14:169.1: 169. (26) Those given for the first (22), excepting happiness (v), come into association with the fifth (26).
vsm2.14:169.2:
(27) And as with the fifth (26), so with the sixth too (27); but the difference here
is promptedness and the inconstant occurrence of stiffness-and-torpor (xliii).
vsm2.14:169.3:
(28) With the seventh (28) should be understood to be associated those given for the fifth (26),
except views (xli); but pride (xliv) is inconstant here.
vsm2.14:169.4:
(29) With the eighth (29) should be understood to be associated those given for the sixth (27),
except views (xli); and here too pride (xliv) is among the inconstant.
vsm2.14:170.1:
170. (30)–(31) As regards the two kinds of unprofitable consciousness rooted in hate, there are, firstly, eighteen associated with
the first (30), that is, eleven constant given in the texts as such (see Dhs § 413), four or-whatever-states, and three inconstant.
vsm2.14:170.2:
Herein the eleven given as such are these: contact (i), volition (ii), applied thought (iii), sustained thought (iv), energy (vi),
life (vii), concentration (viii), consciencelessness (xxxvii), shamelessness (xxxviii), (xlv) hate, delusion (xl).
vsm2.14:170.3: The four or-whatever-states are these: zeal (xxviii), resolution (xxix), agitation (xlii), attention (xxx).
vsm2.14:170.4: The three inconstant are these: (xlvi) envy, (xlvii) avarice, (xlviii) worry.
vsm2.14:171.1: 171. Herein, (xlv) by its means they hate, or it itself hates, or it is just mere hating, thus it is hate (dosa).
vsm2.14:171.2: It has the characteristic of savageness, like a provoked snake.
vsm2.14:171.3: Its function is to spread, like a drop of poison, or its function is to burn up its own support, like a forest fire.
vsm2.14:171.4: It is manifested as persecuting (dūsana), like an enemy who has got his chance.
vsm2.14:171.5: Its proximate cause is the grounds for annoyance (see A V 150).
vsm2.14:171.6: It should be regarded as like stale urine mixed with poison.
vsm2.14:172.2: It has the characteristic of being jealous of other's success.
vsm2.14:172.3: Its function is to be dissatisfied with that.
vsm2.14:172.4: It is manifested as averseness from that.
vsm2.14:172.5: Its proximate cause is another's success.
vsm2.14:172.6: It should be regarded as a fetter.
vsm2.14:173.2: Its characteristic is the hiding of one's own success that has been or can be obtained.
vsm2.14:173.3: Its function is not to bear sharing these with others.
vsm2.14:173.4: It is manifested as shrinking, or it is manifested as meanness.
vsm2.14:173.5: Its proximate cause is one's own success.
vsm2.14:173.6: It should be regarded as a mental disfigurement.
vsm2.14:174.1: 174. (xlviii) The vile (kucchita) that is done (kata) is villainy (kukata). The state of that is worry (kukkucca).
vsm2.14:174.2: It has subsequent regret as its characteristic.
vsm2.14:174.3: Its function is to sorrow about what has and what has not been done.
vsm2.14:174.5: Its proximate cause is what has and what has not been done.
vsm2.14:174.6: It should be regarded as slavery.
vsm2.14:175.1: 175. The rest are of the kind already described.
vsm2.14:175.2:
So these eighteen formations should be understood to come into association with the first
unprofitable consciousness rooted in hate (30).
vsm2.14:175.3:
(31) And as with the first (30), so with the second (31), the only difference, however,
being promptedness and the presence of stiffness and torpor (xliii) among the inconstant.
vsm2.14:176.1:
176. (32)–(33) As regards the two rooted in delusion, firstly: associated with the consciousness
that is associated with uncertainty (32) are the eleven given in the texts as such thus: contact (i), volition (ii),
applied thought (iii), sustained thought (iv), energy (vi), life (vii), (xlix) steadiness of consciousness,
consciencelessness (xxxvii), shamelessness (xxxviii), delusion (xl), (l) uncertainty.
vsm2.14:176.2: The or-whatever-states are these two: agitation (xlii), attention (xxx). And these together total thirteen.
vsm2.14:177.1: 177. Herein, (xlix) steadiness of consciousness is weak concentration (viii) consisting in mere steadiness in occurrence.
vsm2.14:177.2: (l) It is without wish to cure (vigatā cikicchā), thus it is uncertainty (vicikicchā).
vsm2.14:177.3: It has the characteristic of doubt.
vsm2.14:177.5: It is manifested as indecisiveness, or it is manifested as taking various sides.
vsm2.14:177.6: Its proximate cause is unwise attention.
vsm2.14:177.7: It should be regarded as obstructive of theory (see XVII.52).
vsm2.14:177.8: The rest are as already described.
vsm2.14:178.1:
178. (33) The consciousness associated with agitation (33) has the same formations as the consciousness
associated with uncertainty (32), except for uncertainty (1).
vsm2.14:178.2: But with the absence of uncertainty resolution (xxix) arises here.
vsm2.14:178.3: So with that they are likewise thirteen, and concentration (viii) is stronger because of the presence of resolution.
vsm2.14:178.4: Also agitation is given in the texts as such,
vsm2.14:178.5: while resolution (xxix) and attention (xxx) are among the or-whatever-states. Thus should the unprofitable formations be understood.
vsm2.14:179.1:
179. III. As regards the indeterminate, firstly, the resultant indeterminate (34)–(69) are twofold,
classed as those without root-cause and those with root-cause.
vsm2.14:179.2: Those associated with resultant consciousness without root-cause (34)–(41), (50)–(56) are those without root-cause.
vsm2.14:179.3:
Herein, firstly, those associated with the profitable resultant (34) and unprofitable resultant (50)
eye-consciousness are the four given in the texts as such, namely: contact (i), volition (ii), life (vii),
steadiness of consciousness (xlix), which amount to five with attention (xxx) as the only or-whatever-state.
vsm2.14:179.4: These same kinds are associated with ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness (35)–(38), (51)–(54).
vsm2.14:180.1:
180. Those associated with both kinds of resultant mind-element (39), (55) come to eight by adding applied
thought (iii), sustained thought (iv) and resolution (xxix). Likewise those associated with the threefold
mind-consciousness-element with root-cause (40), (41), (56).
vsm2.14:180.2: But here (40) that accompanied by joy should be understood to have happiness (v) also in addition to that.
vsm2.14:181.1: 181. The formations associated with resultant consciousness with root-cause (42)–(49) are those with root-cause.
vsm2.14:181.2:
Of these, firstly, those associated with the sense-sphere resultant consciousness with root-cause
are similar to the formations associated with the eight sense-sphere consciousnesses (1)–(8).
vsm2.14:181.3:
But of the inconstant ones, compassion (xxxii) and gladness (xxxiii) are not among the resultant because they
have living beings as their object. For the resultant ones of the sense-sphere have only limited objects.
vsm2.14:181.4: And not only compassion and gladness but also the three abstinences (xxxiv)–(xxxvi) are not among the resultant;
vsm2.14:181.5: for it is said that "the five training precepts are profitable only" (Vibh 291).
vsm2.14:182.1:
182. (57)–(69) Those associated with the resultant consciousness of the fine- material sphere (57)–(61),
the immaterial sphere (62)–(65), and the supramundane (66)–(69) are similar to the formations
associated with the profitable consciousnesses of those kinds (9)–(21) too.
